Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the warning days, the use-by risk days, how long a supplier declaration stays valid, the days to answer a client and the training warning days.
Keep Products, Ingredients and Recipe lines up to date. Fill the Allergen matrix with yes or no for each product: the allergen count and the list of allergens fill in.
Write the ingredient text and the allergen text of every product on Label texts. A label is ready when all four parts are filled, and a label that gives more days than the product keeps is flagged.
Record every bake on Batches with the code, the quantity and the baker, and every label print on the Label log. The use-by date, the days left and the shelf check fill in.

List every order with an allergy note on Allergy orders and write who checked it and when. A conflict between the allergy and the product is flagged, and the Orders sheet flags the same on open orders.
Write each cross-contact check on Cross-contact checks and each cleaning task on the Cleaning log. Overdue tasks, failed checks and the days since the previous clean show at once.
Keep one row for each ingredient on Supplier declarations with what the supplier declared and the date you checked it. Out of date declarations and differences from your list are flagged.
Write every allergen incident, client question and food complaint on its own sheet with the action and the outcome, so the days open, the days to answer and the refund share fill in.
Use Shelf life rules for the days and the wording by storage, Seasonal range for what is on sale now, Product changes for label updates and Allergen training for the next due dates.

Use the 14 calculators when you answer a client: the allergens of a product, a safe product for an allergy, an order conflict, the use-by date, the batch code, the cross-contact risk and the label order.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link (28 messages). Check your own local rules on allergens, labels and storage.
Read the Allergens and Labels Dashboard and Charts every week: unchecked allergy orders, conflicts, labels not ready, failed checks, overdue cleaning, old declarations, open incidents and complaints.

Deliveries, pick-ups, markets and pop-ups for home bakeries and cake studios
Delivery schedule by zone and time window
every delivery shows its day, zone, time window, driver, km and fee, with a flag for late and failed ones
the stops, the km between them and the minutes at each stop give the total time, the finish time and whether the run fits the driver day
each run shows its cost for each stop against the fee collected, so a zone where the fee does not cover the cost is found
every late or failed delivery keeps its reason, the action taken, the cost of the redo and the credit to offer
orders waiting on the shelf show their slot, whether they are ready, the balance to collect and the hours until the slot
the units you expect to sell and the mix of products give the units of each group to bring, with a safety share on top
Market profit after stall fee and labour
each market shows revenue, goods cost, stall fee and labour, then the profit, the margin and a profit or loss flag
units brought against sold give the sell-through and the cost of what was left, so the next stock plan is based on real sales
every item to pack for a coming market has a quantity, a person and a packed tick, and the units still missing are counted
each invitation shows the units you must sell to break even and how long it has waited, so the answer is made on numbers

Deliveries by day, zone and time window
One row for each delivery with the zone, the time window, the driver, the km and the fee; the on time flag and the fee for each km fill in, so late and failed deliveries stand out.
Delivery runs with the cost for each stop
One row for each run of a driver in one zone with the stops, the km, the hours and the fees collected; the cost of the run, the cost for each stop and whether the fees cover it fill in.
Delivery zones with the fee and the distance
The five delivery zones with the fee you charge and the distance from the kitchen; the fee tool and the orders read the fee from here.
Time windows with the start and the end hour
The four delivery and pick-up windows with the hour each one starts and ends; the pick-up shelf reads the start hour from here.
Pick-ups with the time window and the balance due
One row for each order collected at the kitchen with the time window, the balance still to pay and the day it was collected; the pick-up status fills in, so an order not collected stands out.
The orders due in the last and the next weeks with the way they leave the kitchen; the delivery fee to charge fills in from the zone.
Pick-up shelf with the hours to the slot
One row for each order waiting on the shelf with its slot, whether it is ready and the balance to collect; the hours until the slot starts fill in.
Late and failed deliveries with the cost of the redo
One row for each late or failed delivery with the reason, what was done and the order value; the cost of the redo, the credit to offer and the total loss fill in.
Markets and pop-ups with profit after stall fee and labour
One row for each market or pop-up with the stall fee, hours, units, revenue and costs; the profit, the sell-through (the share of what you brought that you sold) and a profit or loss flag fill in.
Market stock plan with sell-through and leftover cost
One row for each market with the main product brought and sold; the units left, the sell-through and the cost of the leftover fill in, so the next stock plan is based on what sold.
One row for each product sold at a market with the units and the revenue; the price for each unit fills in, so you see what sells at which stall.
Event calendar with the application deadline
One row for each market, fair or pop-up you plan, applied for or did, with the stall fee, the application deadline and the status; the days to the event and the deadline flag fill in.
Market packing list with the items missing
One row for each item to pack for a coming market with the quantity, who packs it and whether it is packed; the event, its date and the units still missing fill in.
Pop-up requests with the break-even units
One row for each invitation to run a stall with the organiser, the date wanted, the stall fee and the hours; the units you must sell to break even and the days waiting for an answer fill in.
Vehicle costs with the cost for each delivery
One row for each month with the fuel and parking, the upkeep and the deliveries made; the vehicle cost and the cost for each delivery fill in.
Delivery feedback with a low rating flag
One row for each rating a client gave a delivery with the comment; the low rating flag fills in, so a bad delivery is followed up the same week.
Driver hours with the deliveries for each hour
One row for each day a driver worked with the hours and the deliveries made; the deliveries for each hour and an overtime flag fill in.
Clients with zone and the market they live near
The clients who order most with their phone, zone and last order, and the market stall that is nearest to them, so a message about a stall reaches the right people.
Products with pack, shelf days, price and cost
The 24 products with the pack, how long they keep, the price and the ingredient and packaging cost of one unit; the market tables read the cost from here.
